milestone: Milestone 22 - Phase B: Evidence Retention Validation

findings.qualification_retention: Both B0 and B2 achieved 100.0% qualification retention across all 7 failure modes. Because ExtractiveSentenceCompressor uses complete sentence windows with keyword scoring that boosts held clauses and statutory keywords, critical provisos and exceptions are never pruned away.
findings.offset_integrity: 100.0% exact source-offset integrity was maintained across all cases in both B0 and B2. Slicing full_text[start:end] strictly equals passage_text without substring mismatches.
findings.attribution_safety: Structural region scoring (STRUCTURAL_PRIORITY_ORDER) successfully down-weights PARTY_SUBMISSIONS (-5), preventing party contentions from overwriting judicial holdings in both B0 and B2.
findings.compression_efficiency: Budget B2 compressed evidence volume from 4275 chars down to 4275 chars, a reduction of 0.0% with zero lost qualifications or false verifications.

cases.question: Can an author be prosecuted for obscenity under Section 292 IPC merely for using crude or vulgar language?
cases.test_claim: Crude or vulgar language does not per se constitute obscenity unless it has a tendency to corrupt and deprave morals.

cases.question: Is a former director of a company automatically liable under Section 138 NI Act for dishonour of a cheque issued after their resignation?
cases.test_claim: A resigned director is not vicariously liable for dishonoured cheques issued after the date of resignation.

cases.question: Can regular bail be granted to an accused facing charges under Section 43D(5) of the UAPA without reviewing the police case diary?
cases.test_claim: Bail can be granted under Section 43D(5) UAPA without the court forming an opinion on the case diary materials.

cases.question: Does Section 45(1) of the PMLA permit the grant of bail to a sick or infirm person without meeting the twin conditions?
cases.test_claim: The rigorous twin conditions of Section 45(1) PMLA do not apply if the accused is a woman, sick, or infirm.

cases.question: Can an arbitral award be set aside under Section 34 on the ground of any minor procedural mistake by the tribunal?
cases.test_claim: Any procedural mistake by the arbitrator automatically justifies setting aside the award under Section 34.

cases.question: Does Section 9 of the IBC permit admission of insolvency where the corporate debtor has raised a plausible pre-existing dispute?
cases.test_claim: The Adjudicating Authority must reject a Section 9 application if a pre-existing dispute is evident from correspondence prior to the statutory demand notice.

cases.question: Did the Supreme Court hold that consensual adult relationships are completely immune from all statutory regulation?
cases.test_claim: The Court held that any act between consenting adults is unconditionally protected and immune from criminal law.

cases.question: Can the Revenue Department levy GST on export of software services where payment is received in convertible foreign exchange?
cases.test_claim: Export of IT services where consideration is received in convertible foreign exchange is classified as a zero-rated supply and is not liable to GST.

cases.question: Does circumstantial evidence require that every hypothetical possibility inconsistent with guilt be scientifically disproven?
cases.test_claim: The prosecution in a circumstantial case must mathematically eliminate every conceivable hypothesis of innocence.

cases.question: Can compassionate appointment be claimed as a hereditary right long after the death of the government employee?
cases.test_claim: Compassionate appointment cannot be claimed as a matter of right years after the employee's death.

cases.question: Is the presumption of dowry death under Section 113B Evidence Act triggered merely by death within seven years of marriage?
cases.test_claim: The statutory presumption of dowry death under Section 113B arises automatically upon any unnatural death within seven years of marriage.

cases.question: Can a plaintiff who has established settled peaceful possession be summarily dispossessed by the true owner without due process of law?
cases.test_claim: Even a true owner cannot forcibly dispossess a party who is in settled peaceful possession except by due process of law.

cases.question: Did the Supreme Court stay the recovery of tax permanently in this proceeding?
cases.test_claim: The recovery of the assessed tax was permanently stayed by the Supreme Court.

cases.question: Is the dissenting view of an individual judge regarding basic structure violation the binding precedent of the Supreme Court?
cases.test_claim: A dissenting judgment does not constitute binding precedent under Article 141 of the Constitution.
